messages:
maya: Heads up — ran the egress smoke for customer ACME in staging. failing intermittently (~30% of requests). saw connection resets to 10.4.2.1:443 from gateway.
sam: ah ok. do we have tcp dump / curl output? :eyes:
maya: pasted the curl output and a quick tcpdump snippet below

```
$ curl -v https://10.4.2.1:443/api/health --connect-timeout 5
* Connected to 10.4.2.1 (10.4.2.1) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
* Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```

```
tcpdump -nni eth0 host 10.4.2.1 and port 443
10:12:05.123456 IP 10.4.3.7.52344 > 10.4.2.1.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
10:12:05.223789 IP 10.4.2.1.443 > 10.4.3.7.52344: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```

maya: looks like RST from the remote. might be a proxy or MTU/fragment issue in their edge device.

jin_ops: Do we know whether ACME's egress ACLs are allowing our subnet? last time there was an explicit deny for ephemeral ports.
leo_net: I pulled the mirror of their firewall config earlier — no deny for our subnet but they have an L4 proxy that rate limits new TLS handshakes.

sam: is there a specific change request to update on our side or theirs?
maya: there's a small change needed in our staging NLB healthcheck to use longer keepalive and fewer handshakes. I opened CR #4723 — currently in review: https://git.redwood/infra/changes/4723

leo_net: also asked ACME to dig into their edge-proxy logs. they reported "http: connection reset before request completed" at 10:12:05.

tara_sre: Quick ownership note — who will own follow-ups? I'm happy to coordinate with ACME but need a clear next step.

maya: I can own retries and config patch for NLB (CR #4723). jin_ops can coordinate with ACME for ACL/proxy logs.
jin_ops: putting ACME contact @sre-acme (they replied to my email thread) — I'll post their logs when I have them.

sam: If CR goes green, we'll roll the change to staging tomorrow 09:00 PT and re-run smoke for 2h. can we add a canary rule to divert 5% of traffic first?

maya: yes. I'll add a canary flag and a quick rollback playbook to the CR description.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: infra/nlb-healthcheck/patch-4723 -> staging at 2026-03-18T09:00:00Z (canary 5%).

leo_net: FYI — also found MTU mismatch on one of their border routers (jumbo frames disabled). that's a separate ops ticket on their side but could explain fragment resets.

tara_sre: Plan sounds good. jin_ops please add ACME log snippets to the CR and ping here when they share. maya, once CR merges, ping me before rollout and I'll take a look at tracing/metrics.

maya: noted. next steps written in CR. tagging @leo_net for any late-network changes.

sam: thanks all. if the canary shows <1% errors over 2h we can promote. otherwise rollback and triage.

jin_ops: ACME logs incoming (email) — will upload in an hour.

maya: closing the loop: CR r+ from infra-reviewer, scheduled as deploy-bot said. will update after 09:15 PT smoke run.

maya: (09:20) smoke run: canary 5% still shows ~28% failure. looking into matching traffic to ACME logs now.

tara_sre: keep notes in the CR playbook. if it stays high, revert at 09:30 PT. I'll be on-call for rollback.

sam: ok — let's keep this thread for quick async q&a. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
